# Stereo models

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_docs.py from the model cards; do not edit. -->

71 stereo models. Each section says what the model is, whether it may be used commercially and how fast it is; licences and checks are under Details.

Input: a rectified left / right image pair. Output: a disparity map (pixels, left view).

Measured on RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130; `fastforks bench MODEL --size HxW` measures yours. The summary uses one input, 994x1482: kernels time with its speed-up over the faster original run, and kernels peak reserved memory with its ratio to the smaller original one. Where measured (one variant per family), a variant's table also lists portable under `torch.compile` and the fp16 TensorRT engine of portable ([export](../export.md); memory: the engine's device memory + torch's peak). – = not measured; no kernels = the family has no kernels backend (reason under its table). Reserved memory is the allocator's cache: kernels (CUDA graphs, cuDNN workspaces) can reserve a few percent to some tens of percent more than portable at the same allocated peak. The accuracy column is lower-is-better (ETH3D bad > 1 px (%)).

Other devices: [Apple M1 Pro 16 GB](../devices/apple-m1-pro-16gb.md), [Apple M1 Pro 16 GB (MLX)](../devices/apple-m1-pro-mlx-16gb.md), [NVIDIA L4](../devices/l4-22gb.md), [NVIDIA L40S](../devices/l40s-44gb.md), [NVIDIA A10](../devices/a10-22gb.md), [NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB](../devices/a100-sxm4-40gb.md), [NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000](../devices/rtx-pro-6000-96gb.md); [across devices](../benchmarks.md#other-devices).

## AANet

A stereo network that aggregates matching costs with sparse deformable sampling across scales, trained on synthetic SceneFlow data.

Commercial use: yes.

| variant | input | backend | time (ms) | peak memory (MiB, allocated / reserved) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `aanet-sceneflow` | Middlebury 2014 half (994x1482) | original (fp32)<br>original<br>portable<br>kernels<br>portable + torch.compile<br>TensorRT fp16 | 289<br>178<br>140<br>101<br>91.8<br>91.2 | 1785 / 1962<br>1000 / 1126<br>845 / 986<br>536 / 644<br>754 / 928<br>602 / 620 |
| `aanet-plus-sceneflow` | Middlebury 2014 half (994x1482) | original (fp32)<br>original<br>portable<br>kernels<br>portable + torch.compile<br>TensorRT fp16 | 263<br>194<br>159<br>88.9<br>143<br>202 | 3618 / 3896<br>3652 / 3784<br>1142 / 1278<br>813 / 920<br>3020 / 3716<br>1786 / 1834 |

- `aanet-plus-sceneflow` original (fp32) 994x1482: deformable conv via torchvision.ops.deform_conv2d (original CUDA extension not built)
- `aanet-plus-sceneflow` original 994x1482: torch.autocast(fp16) around the forward; deformable conv via torchvision.ops.deform_conv2d (original CUDA extension not built)

- `aanet-plus-sceneflow` load / first call: original 0.15 s / 0.701 s (375x1242), portable 0.16 s / 0.166† s, kernels 0.2† s / 0.09† s
- † measured in the speed sweep after the portable load (or an earlier size) in the same process: file cache and kernels are warm, so the time is lower than a fresh start.
- Protocol, median of 5 after 3 warm-up, uint8 CUDA input (synthetic for bench_inputs sizes), card defaults; gc before each load; peak = max over the first call and the timed calls

### Parity

CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 0.002 vs the original. GPU, float16 (the default), portable and kernels: mean |diff| <= 0.02 px and p99 <= 0.25 px.

| variant | kernels error vs original, mean / p99 | GPU, torch | kernels used |
|---|---|---|---|
| `aanet-sceneflow` | 0.00403 / 0.04845 | RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130 | `cudnn_hacc@cudnn92400`, `cutlass_conv@988138e042cb:sm_120`, `deform_conv@a38662ea1bfc:sm_120`, `igev@f075827d68c6:sm_120` |
| `aanet-plus-sceneflow` | 0.00295 / 0.02185 | RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130 | `cudnn_hacc@cudnn92400`, `cutlass_conv@988138e042cb:sm_120`, `deform_conv@a38662ea1bfc:sm_120`, `igev@f075827d68c6:sm_120` |

### Limitations

- Only the SceneFlow checkpoints of AANet and AANet+ are included; the original code's KITTI fine-tunes are not.
- At 375x1242 AANet is launch-bound: portable is about as fast as the original code. At 994x1482 portable is faster but allocates more memory.

## BridgeDepth

A stereo network that aligns Depth Anything V2 features with NMRF-style disparity proposals. Non-commercial weights.

Commercial use: **no** (weights: CC-BY-NC-4.0).

### Measured

Use all 15 trainingH pairs with a shared centre crop and edge padding. Score valid non-occluded pixels and exclude right-image correspondences outside the crop. Average the per-pair endpoint error and share of pixels with error above 2 pixels. Original = the original code named under Details, same checkpoint and protocol.

CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 0.002 vs the original. GPU, float16 (the default), portable and kernels: mean |diff| <= 0.02 px and p99 <= 0.25 px. On real pairs up to 720x1280 the limits are mean 0.06 / p99 1.0 (precision-sensitive there, see Limitations).

| variant | kernels error vs original, mean / p99 | GPU, torch | kernels used |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bridgedepth-sf` | 0.00036 / 0.00123 | RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130 | `fastbb@7d058322634d:sm_120` |
| `bridgedepth-rvc-pretrain` | 0.00053 / 0.00327 | RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130 | `fastbb@7d058322634d:sm_120` |

### Limitations

- ONNX Runtime resolves top-k ties differently from PyTorch on noise pairs: bridgedepth-sf differs by up to 0.010 px (mean 0.001) on a synthetic textured pair.
- At fixed 375 x 1242, the FP32 standalone monocular TensorRT branch took 284 ms on both checkpoints versus 324 to 325 ms for paired portable FP32. The stereo branch stayed in PyTorch. The largest individual NOC endpoint-error change was 0.0023 px across the two 15-pair Middlebury checks.

</details>

### Parity

CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 0.002 vs the original. GPU, float16 (the default), portable and kernels: mean |diff| <= 0.02 px and p99 <= 0.25 px. On real pairs up to 720x1280 the limits are mean 0.25 / p99 5.0 (precision-sensitive there, see Limitations).

- For the Middlebury weights, the nominal TensorRT plan failed to allocate an execution context. A smaller 384 x 640 ONNX export with 32 iterations exceeded the 228-second limit both with and without ONNX optimization.
- The fixed 375 x 1242 FP32 TensorRT measurement uses the MobileNetV2 feature pyramid with eager stereo inference. Across all 15 Middlebury trainingH center crops, the largest change in non-occluded disparity EPE was 0.00098 px. Latency was 3.697 s versus 3.704 s for portable.

### Limitations

- CUDA output (float16, kernels, float32 with PyTorch's default TF32 convolutions) differs from the CPU by ~0.2 px mean / 4 px p99 at 720x1280: the argmin flips on near-equal tile costs. Full float32 (`torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32 = False`) matches the CPU to 0.00002 px.
- The weights are the authors' frozen TensorFlow graphs read without TensorFlow; the FlyingThings and Middlebury d160 / d288 graphs are not included.
- The original code is TensorFlow (frozen graph run with TensorFlow 2.21 on the GPU); its time is the upstream row, its memory is the TensorFlow peak (TensorFlow has no reserved-memory counter).

- Portable LAS2-H at 375 x 1242 is faster than the original code (35.6 vs 36.4 ms) but peaks 13 MB (3.7 %) higher (365 vs 352 MB). Kernels at 994 x 1482 allocate less than the original (917 vs 1022 MB) but reserve more (1248 vs 1084 MB): graph / cuDNN workspace blocks.

### Limitations

- Only the two SynLarge checkpoints (S, B) are included; DAv2L-5 and the Real / KITTI / Middlebury fine-tunes are not.
- On the 994 x 1482 FP16 profile, portable WAFT-B groups the attention heads to save about 2 GiB of peak allocation at comparable latency. Kernels runs about three times faster than portable and uses under half its peak allocation.
- WAFT-Stereo-B kernels runs its ViT attention with fp16 accumulation: single attention outputs differ from fp32 by up to 34 % (relative), but end-to-end ETH3D / Middlebury-H accuracy matches the fp32 original (EPE 0.163 / 0.728).
- The standalone FP32 TensorRT engine at 384 x 1248 matched portable FP32 at 2.904% D1 over 200 KITTI pairs. Median time was 1,208 ms with TensorRT and 381 ms portable. The default FP16 TensorRT exporter remains gated.

</details>
